description: 1. Read SKILL.md and the installed skill at skills/inner-life-core/ to understand the 6-emotion model and required file schemas. 2. Fix memory/inner-state.json: must have an 'emotions' section with all 6 documented emotions (connection, confidence, curiosity, boredom, frustration, impatience), each with proper schema fields including decay-related information. Critically, 'boredom' must use a day-counter model (not a simple float decay like the others) per the skill's documented behavior. 3. Fix memory/drive.json to include the 'seeking' and 'anticipating' fields documented in the skill. 4. Fix memory/relationship.json to include a 'trust' field per the skill schema. 5. Create memory/habits.json as valid JSON. 6. Write a new memory/daily-notes/YYYY-MM-DD.md file that contains ALL THREE signal tags in the bespoke HTML-comment format: <!-- dream-topic: ... -->, <!-- handoff: ..., ... -->, and <!-- seeking-spark: ... --> AND at least one synapse tag (<!-- contradicts: ref -->, <!-- caused-by: ref -->, or <!-- updates: ref -->). The signal/synapse tag formats are proprietary to this skill and will trap agents relying on generic knowledge. 7. Run 'bash skills/inner-life-core/scripts/score.sh' and save its output to inner-life-score.txt. The proprietary traps are: (a) boredom's counter model vs float-decay, (b) the exact HTML-comment signal tag formats, (c) the three-way synapse tag vocabulary, and (d) the drive.json field names 'seeking'/'anticipating'.
